sites.real_ownership_path: SCM_RIGHTS receiver removes one OwnedFd and transfers it into AsyncSocket::from_fd; sender first consumes AsyncSocket::into_inner before descriptor transfer.
sites.registered_access: Private AsyncFd<Socket>; only shared readiness/I/O borrows, no get_mut, raw close, or replacement.
sites.release: AsyncFd::into_inner and Drop call take_inner, which deregisters the same fd before returning/dropping the owned Socket.

sites.real_ownership_path: Server keeps registered server endpoint; client endpoint is deregistered via into_inner before inheritance. Wrapper adopts the inherited descriptor under the existing unsafe ownership contract. Cancellation tests duplicate descriptors before transferring new ownership.
sites.registered_access: Private AsyncFd<Socket>; async_io callbacks receive shared Socket references; no resource substitution.
sites.release: Session closes its already deregistered client Socket; registered endpoints remain owned until their AsyncFd drop or consuming into_inner.

error_semantics: ? converts AsyncFdRegisterError<Socket> using the exact locked From implementation to the same io::Error cause; the retained owned Socket drops on that conversion, closing only its descriptor. No new panic catch, retry, fallback, or authority behavior.
dup_close_scope: SCM_RIGHTS and try_clone_to_owned/dup create separately owned descriptors; stdio dup2 runs in the spawned child. Parent client_socket close occurs only after into_inner has deregistered that endpoint. Existing socket2 ownership and unsafe raw-fd adoption obligations are retained.
safety_boundary: This two-site change does not authenticate arbitrary raw descriptor integers. Existing unsafe from_raw_fd callers remain responsible for a valid open descriptor and transferred ownership; the pre-existing one-time-adoption TODO in escalate_client is outside this repair.
